# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a **250-500 Wh** unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, camera batteries, and a CPAP for a weekend. Go bigger only if you want to run a fridge or cooler.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290 Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288 Wh, 8.3 lb, 300 W AC) is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold at Amazon and other retailers. [PowerStationGearLab guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286 Wh, 600 W AC) has double the Jackery's inverter output and can expand to 572 Wh. Same guide.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288 Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the version with AC outlets, not the "DC" variant. Same guide.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268 Wh, 600 W AC) is the budget pick. Same guide.

Note that OutdoorGearLab, which buys and lab-tests its units, scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low against larger models. They're fine for phones and laptops, but the small class has limits. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Longer trips, a 12V fridge, or an electric cooler
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It measured 1,710 Wh usable, weighs 39 lb, and was recently found for under $900 on Amazon (list $1,499). It has no battery expansion. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 on sale. It's compact but has a noisy fan and limited capacity. Same page.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070 Wh, 23.8 lb) is the van and overland pick in the first guide. TechRadar also names it best for camping. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's best for camping at $1,079-1,199. It's IP65-rated and weighs just under 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Mid-size option with a direct buy link
**Bluetti AC180** has 1,152 Wh of LiFePO4 and an 1,800 W inverter, and weighs about 16 kg (35 lb). It lists at $499 and is $474.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the site tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. The $499 price is the station alone, and the 5-year warranty requires proof of purchase from an official store. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. [Product details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

## My pick
- **Light weekend trips:** the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, or the EcoFlow River 3 Plus if you want more AC output.
- **Tight budget:** the Bluetti EB3A or Anker C300.
- **Fridge, cooler, or multi-day trips:** the Anker C1000 Gen 2 or Bluetti AC180, or the Jackery 2000 v2 if you can spend more.

The search results didn't include direct store links for most of these, so I've linked the review pages. Check current prices at the retailer, since sales are heating up ahead of Black Friday.
